findings.title: plans_still_posting counts only the withdrawn ROW's plans, so a firm that ever restated or re-recorded its instruction is told 'Nothing was running under it' while schedules keep posting
findings.evidence: 0362 SB counts on `ap.authority_ref ->> 'id' = v_row.id::text` (packages/db/migrations/0362_standing_instruction_agent_read.sql:379-385), i.e. on the ROW being withdrawn. But 0338's record door is version-forward: read off the LIVE catalog, clara.record_firm_standing_instruction supersedes the live row whenever the reason OR the recording member differs (`if found and v_existing.reason = v_reason and v_existing.recorded_by = v_actor then ... else update ... set withdrawn_at = now(), withdraw_reason = 'superseded by a restated standing instruction' ... insert ...`). Plans authorised before the restatement keep citing the SUPERSEDED row. DRIVEN on clara_c01 through the estate's own doors (scratchpad probe3.mjs): alice records R1 = f698c59b-53ac-44d6-8c4a-a82a3aa49338; the real close_prep wake wrapper writes plan e1572d5d-ee97-43a8-abd0-5bb741471d50 with authority_ref {"id":"f698c59b...","kind":"firm_standing_instruction","instruction_key":"prepayment_schedule_at_close","wake_kind":"close_prep"}; alice restates the reason -> R1 withdrawn as 'superseded by a restated standing instruction', R2 = 502bfbda-de2f-40b1-a7ed-853bf83289c1 inserted; alice withdraws -> receipt {"instruction_id":"502bfbda...","plans_still_posting":0}; the plan re-read as root is still {"id":"e1572d5d...","status":"active"}. apps/web/components/firm-admin/standing-instructions-card.tsx:149 then renders apps/web/messages/en.json:7754's =0 arm: "Nothing was running under it, so nothing keeps posting." That is the exact false belief #1147 exists to remove (issue #1147: 'A firm that takes an instruction back reasonably believes it stopped something'). No cell covers a superseded row: p1147.withdraw.counts and p1147.withdraw.counts_only_what_still_posts each record the instruction exactly once, and neither the migration header nor waveK-lane01-ticket1147.md mentions restatement.
findings.required_fix: Count the firm's instruction rather than the row. Every standing-instruction plan already carries authority_ref ->> 'instruction_key' (89 of 89 rows on clara_c01, measured), so the predicate becomes `ap.authority_ref ->> 'instruction_key' = v_key` (or the id IN the set of this firm's rows for that key), with `ap.firm_id = v_firm and ap.status = 'active' and ap.authority_kind = 'standing_instruction'` unchanged. Add a cell that records, authorises a plan, RESTATES the reason, withdraws, and asserts plans_still_posting = 1. If the orchestrator rules the receipt must stay row-scoped, then the =0 message must stop asserting that nothing keeps posting.

findings.kind: correctness / wrong sentence on the success path
findings.title: The new document-page section renders for EVERY payroll summary, so a payslip that posted correctly is told 'This payslip was not posted again -- decide whether this is a correction or a re-upload'
findings.evidence: apps/web/components/documents/payroll-posting-section.tsx gates only on documentKind === 'payroll_summary' (line 57) and then renders state.sentence verbatim (lines 91-97) with no test on verdict, rung or the duplicate's scope; apps/web/components/documents/document-detail.tsx:403 mounts it immediately under the liveClaim / noLiveClaim line on the ACCOUNTING tab. clara._payroll_posting_verdict answers verdict='blocked', rung='no_duplicate_entry' for a payslip whose OWN entry exists (scope same_document, via clara._document_posting_entry(v_client, p_document)), and that sentence is written for a re-file attempt. DRIVEN end to end on clara_c01 (scratchpad probe2.mjs): seedPayrollChart + readPayrollDoc(month 2027-06) posts entry 72eb326d-6c88-478e-8a40-e7d5de67eaf2 (approved, memo 'Payroll run June 2027') from the document; clara.get_payroll_posting_state, called through humanQuery as firm A's VIEWER carol, answers sentence = "Payroll run June 2027 is already posted (Payroll run June 2027, 2027-06-30). This payslip was not posted again -- open that entry to decide whether this is a correction or a re-upload." The ordinary success page therefore reads 'A posted entry of <client> currently stands on this document.' followed by the heading 'Payroll posting' and a sentence saying the payslip was not posted and inviting the reader to decide whether it is a correction or a re-upload - about its own entry. The ticket's scope is 'a document page that wants to say this payslip did not post because ...'; none of the five cells in payroll-posting-section.test.tsx drives a posted or a ready verdict.
findings.required_fix: Decide what the page says when the verdict is not a blocked-before-posting state: render nothing when the duplicate the verdict names is this document's own entry (the door does not project the duplicate scope today, so either project it or gate on the entries the page already holds), and render nothing for verdict === 'ready'. Add a component cell for a posted payslip and one for a ready verdict.

findings.kind: guard weakened on a false equivalence
findings.title: The amended p1050.doors.shape census admits a machine-lane WRITE twin: 'STABLE, therefore it cannot write' is false once the body calls a VOLATILE helper
findings.evidence: packages/db/tests/prepayment-close-standing-instruction.test.mjs:1122 replaces #1050's exact refusal (assert.deepEqual(kin.rows, []) - no wake_%firm_standing_instruction% name at all, anywhere in the schema) with `const unlawful = kin.rows.filter((r) => !r.is_read || !r.agent || r.writers)`, justified by the new comment: 'STABLE (Postgres refuses every INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE inside a non-volatile function, so such a body CANNOT write)'. PostgreSQL refuses a data-modifying STATEMENT written directly inside a non-volatile function; it does not stop that function calling a VOLATILE one that writes. PROVEN on clara_c01 inside a transaction that was rolled back (scratchpad stable_write.sql): created clara._adv_volatile_writer(uuid,text) (VOLATILE, inserts into clara.firm_standing_instructions) and clara.wake_record_firm_standing_instruction(uuid,text) declared `stable security definer`, owner clara_fn_owner, revoked from public, granted to clara_agent_ro alone. The amended census's own query then answers {proname: wake_record_firm_standing_instruction, is_read: true, agent: true, writers: false}, so `unlawful` is empty and the cell stays GREEN; the same call returned a new instruction id and `select count(*) from clara.firm_standing_instructions where reason = 'ADVERSARIAL: a STABLE body that wrote'` = 1. After the rollback, `select count(*) from pg_proc ... in ('_adv_volatile_writer','wake_record_firm_standing_instruction')` = 0. The wall #1050 owns - no machine lane may RECORD or WITHDRAW a standing instruction - is now satisfiable by a machine-lane write door.
findings.required_fix: Add the fact that actually closes it: refuse any name in the family whose prosrc reaches a VOLATILE clara body, or list the lawful READ signatures explicitly (the shape 0363's own p1148.acl.census uses, which enumerates every clara_% role from pg_roles and asserts the reached set exactly). At minimum delete the sentence claiming STABLE implies the body cannot write, because that claim is the amendment's whole justification.

findings.title: A close_prep run in flight at the moment of withdrawal lands an active plan that the receipt has already counted as absent
findings.evidence: 0362 SB's header claims the count is taken 'After the stamp, inside the same transaction, so what it reports is the world the withdrawal leaves behind rather than the one it found'. It reports the withdrawing transaction's SNAPSHOT. The wake arm of clara._prepayment_schedule_core resolves the instruction with a plain `select fsi.id, fsi.recorded_by ... where fsi.withdrawn_at is null limit 1` (live body read - no FOR SHARE, no FOR UPDATE), and the withdraw door's own `for update` is on the instruction row only, so nothing serialises the two. DRIVEN with TWO real connections (scratchpad probe4.mjs): connection W opens a transaction, sets role clara_wake_interactive under a real close_prep credential and calls clara.wake_establish_prepayment_schedule -> plan 92c820ab-91e8-4c7f-bc2e-16f8db54c3f2 written and NOT committed; a second connection withdraws as alice and commits -> receipt plans_still_posting = 0; W then commits and the plan reads status='active' citing that instruction. The card says 'Nothing was running under it, so nothing keeps posting.' Narrower than ADV-01 (it needs an overlapping unattended run) but the same false sentence.
findings.required_fix: Either take a FOR SHARE / FOR KEY SHARE on the instruction row in the wake arm so the two serialise (outside this ticket's scope - raise it as a successor item), or stop the receipt claiming to describe the world after the withdrawal and word the =0 case so it does not assert that nothing keeps posting.

findings.kind: assertion weaker than its own claim
findings.title: 0362's tail ACL check is a four-name denylist, not the allowlist its comment claims; a grant to any other clara role passes
findings.evidence: packages/db/migrations/0362_standing_instruction_agent_read.sql:471 tests `v_acl ~ 'clara_runtime=|clara_authenticated=|clara_wake_|clara_agent_chat_ro='` plus a PUBLIC arm, under a comment saying 'Read off the ACL rather than asked role by role, so a grant to a role this file never names is caught too'. PROVEN on clara_c01 inside a rolled-back transaction (scratchpad re4.sql): after `grant execute on function clara.wake_get_firm_standing_instruction(text) to clara_freeform_ro`, the tail's first check does not fire (the clara_agent_ro entry is still there), its second does not fire either, and has_function_privilege('clara_freeform_ro', ...) = true - the tail would have applied happily. This cluster carries clara_freeform_ro, clara_stripe_webhook, clara_invite_preview, clara_agent_read_login and clara_auth_wall, none of which the regex names; clara_agent_chat_ro, which it does name, is not a role that exists here. p1147.read.acl has the same shape (a fixed four-role loop). By contrast #1148's p1148.acl.census enumerates `pg_roles where rolname like 'clara\_%'` and asserts the reached set is exactly ['clara_authenticated'].
findings.required_fix: Assert the ACL positively: read every clara_% role from pg_roles plus public and require the reached set to be exactly {clara_agent_ro}, in the 0362 tail and in p1147.read.acl - 0363's own shape.

findings.title: The read door names the recording member as a bare user uuid, and no wake-lane door resolves a uuid to a person
findings.evidence: 0362 SA projects recorded_by as the raw uuid, and waveK-lane01-ticket1147.md's successor contract carries it as "recorded_by": "<user uuid>". Catalog census on clara_c01: of the 11 clara.wake_get_% doors, ZERO project a display name (no clara.wake_% body matches '%display_name%', '%full_name%' or '%users u%'). The chat tool the next cut builds can therefore say that an instruction stands and when, but cannot say WHO recorded it without inventing a name or dropping the field, although the brief lists 'the recording member' as one of the four projections.
findings.required_fix: Not blocking. Either project the member's display name beside the uuid in a later cut, or state in the successor contract that the tool must not attempt to name the person.

summary: Six adversarial findings, three of them major. No tenancy hole and no floor regression was found on either new door: #1148's wrapper walls on clara.documents.firm_id before it reads anything and answers one CLR11 both for a foreign document and for an unminted uuid, and #1147's wake read takes no firm argument at all and rides a credential that clara.wake_context() re-validates as an ACTIVE bookkeeper+ on every use. The three majors are about what the two halves SAY. The withdrawal receipt counts the withdrawn ROW rather than the firm's instruction, so a firm that restated it is told 'Nothing was running under it, so nothing keeps posting' while an amortisation schedule keeps posting (ADV-01, driven through the estate's own doors). The new document-page section renders for every payroll summary, so a payslip that posted correctly is told it 'was not posted again' and invited to decide whether it is a correction or a re-upload (ADV-02, driven end to end). And the amended p1050.doors.shape census rests on 'STABLE, therefore it cannot write', which a STABLE body calling a VOLATILE helper disproves - a machine-lane WRITE twin of the standing-instruction door now passes that census (ADV-03, proven inside a transaction that was rolled back). Two minors (a withdrawal / close_prep race with the same false sentence, and a tail ACL denylist that misses five of this cluster's roles) and one note (recorded_by is a uuid no wake door can resolve).
